speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You are up. The floor was busy at one. Breakfast is threepence if you eat it, and threepence if you look at it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will eat it. I sat too long, and the page is no better for that.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The porridge is by the salt. Gib is on the thin book again. I will not lift him. He bites the honest hand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him. The book can bear a cat. There is nothing under the rule that he can spoil.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: A cat chooses the small book because the small book is warm. He has no opinion of the sentence.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I have an opinion of the hour. Church is at nine. You will wash. There is ink on the finger, and it is yesterday's.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Yesterday's ink. I am not opening the page before church.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Mistress says a man who writes at one looks boiled on Sunday. She said gooseberries. I am only saying you should eat.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I said it, and I meant it. Mark me. The porridge will not wait on a king.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The king can wait. He was still coming down when I left him.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: Then he is where you left him. A page does not walk in the night. I have seen cloth do worse.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Cloth is Gillis's business. Kings are yours, and they are not mine until you tell them properly, which you will not do with a spoon in your hand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will not tell him. He came down a wall. That is the whole of it, and it is not finished.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Down a wall is something a person can see. Is there a lady in it?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No lady. A wall, and a man, and the bottom of the wall not yet on the leaf.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. A lady before church is a distraction, and I am already supplying the sermon. Eat.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: I will eat too. The loom is quiet today. Sunday is for the feet to stop.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gib has put his paw on the line you ruled. I still will not lift him.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The line is the rule. He may sit on it. I wrote nothing under it, and I am not writing it now.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then the book is shut enough. Wash the finger. I will not walk into St Helen's beside a man who looks as if he slept in the ink.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I slept in the bed. The ink was before. Threepence, Mistress. I am eating.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: There is bread if the porridge is not enough. I did not measure it. Mistress measured it on another Sunday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A finger and a half short of the notch, and the price was a penny.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And I am not measuring it again at this table. Bread is bread until I say otherwise. Church. Wash. And no candle tonight past a decent hour.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: A decent hour is a good order. I can keep it. The shuttle will not mind.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I can keep the hour. I cannot promise the page will. Today I will let it alone.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Let it alone until after your supper, whatever supper you have bought yourself. This house is quiet after nine. Mark me.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will keep Gib off the porridge, if he ever leaves the book.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave him the book. I am done with both until evening.
